1352.overview: This exercise focuses on strengthening the erector spinae muscles of the lower back. It's a bodyweight movement suitable for individuals looking to improve spinal stability and posture.

1353.overview: A powerful, full-body exercise that engages the core, shoulders, and legs. This explosive movement improves power, coordination, and cardiovascular endurance. Best suited for intermediate to advanced individuals.

1355.overview: The one arm against wall is an isometric exercise used to activate the latissimus dorsi. It is beneficial for establishing a mind-muscle connection and warming up the back muscles.

Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the entire range of motion.
1356.variations:

Use a neutral grip to target the middle trapezius muscle.
Incorporate isometric holds at the top of the movement to increase time under tension.

1366.overview: This exercise trains the muscles of the spine and is suitable for individuals looking to improve their flexibility and strength in the back. It can be modified to suit different fitness levels.

Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears.

1367.overview: The wide grip rear pull-up is a challenging back exercise that emphasizes the upper back muscles and rear deltoids. It's best suited for intermediate to advanced individuals seeking to enhance their back width and posture.

1368.overview: Ankle circles are a simple mobility exercise that loosens the ankle joint and activates stabilizing muscles, preparing the lower legs for more intense activity. Keep the knee of the moving leg stable; all motion should come from the ankle.
Complete full circles, aiming for a smooth, controlled motion.
Avoid any painful range; stop if you feel discomfort.
Perform the exercise slowly to maximize joint lubrication.
1368.variations:
Ankle pumps (up‑and‑down movement) for a change in stimulus
Alphabet ankle circles tracing the letters of the alphabet
Resistance‑band ankle circles for added load

1369.overview: This exercise targets the calf muscles, requiring engagement of the ankles and feet. It's suitable for those who want to strengthen their lower legs and improve their ankle stability. To perform this exercise, you should be comfortable with balancing on a flat surface.

Focus on squeezing your calf muscles at the top of the movement.
Avoid using momentum to raise your heels.

Calf raise on a step or platform

1370.overview: Performing calf raises on the floor with a barbell engages the gastrocnemius and soleus while also challenging balance and ankle stability. 1370.exerciseTips:
Keep a slight bend in the knees to avoid locking the joint.
Rise onto the toes fully to achieve a complete range of motion.
Control the descent to maintain tension on the calf muscles.
Engage the core to keep the torso stable.

Focus on using your calf muscles to lift your heels upwards.

1373.overview: The bodyweight standing calf raise focuses on building strength and endurance in the calf muscles, specifically the gastrocnemius and soleus. Keep your back flat and posture strict throughout the movement.
Squeeze the towel tightly to maximize forearm engagement.
Drive your elbow back and up rather than pulling with your arm only.

Single-arm dumbbell row
Seated cable row
Resistance band row

with ankle weight

2133.overview: The farmer's walk is a highly functional full-body exercise that effectively builds grip strength, core stability, and overall muscular endurance. Trap bar carry
Kettlebell farmer's walk

2135.overview: The weighted front plank increases the difficulty of a standard plank by adding external resistance. This exercise is excellent for enhancing core strength and stability, suitable for intermediate trainees.

2136.overview: This exercise targets the shoulders and triceps, and is a great option for those looking to improve their overall upper body strength and shoulder stability. It's a beginner-level exercise that suits those who have a good understanding of proper press form.
2136.exerciseTips:
Focus on using your shoulders to press the dumbbells overhead.
Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Use a slow and controlled movement to avoid injury.

Dumbbell snatch press
Dumbbell overhead press with rotation

2137.overview: Targeting the deltoids, this exercise aims to build overall shoulder strength. It's suitable for anyone looking to improve their shoulder stability and power. However, it does require a moderate level of technical skill.
2137.exerciseTips:
Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain control and stability.
Avoid using momentum to lift the dumbbells and focus on controlled movements.
Don't swing your shoulders or arch your back, as this can put unnecessary strain on your muscles.

2138.overview: This exercise targets the cardiovascular system and works multiple muscle groups, particularly the legs. It's suitable for individuals of all fitness levels, from beginner to advanced.

Keep your back straight and core engaged to maintain proper posture.

Avoid bouncing or jerking movements on the pedals.

high-intensity interval training (HIIT) on stationary bike
stationary bike hill sprints

2139.overview: The hands bike, or upper body ergometer, provides a great cardiovascular workout for the upper body, shoulders, and arms. It's an excellent option for individuals needing to rest their lower body or to add variety to their cardio routine.

Alternating arm cycling
Reverse cycling
One-arm cycling

2141.overview: This exercise trains the cardiovascular system and is suitable for individuals looking to improve their endurance and burn calories. It can be modified to suit different fitness levels.

Adjust the resistance level to challenge yourself.

Incline training: Increase the incline of the machine to target different muscle groups.

2142.overview: This exercise utilizes a SkiErg machine to provide a full-body cardiovascular workout, primarily engaging the upper body, core, and legs. It's excellent for building endurance and strength.

2143.overview: The 'Around the World' exercise is a shoulder mobility and stability movement that circles the weights around the body. It keeps constant tension on the deltoids and traps while improving joint range of motion. This standing variation challenges the core to maintain stability throughout the circular path.
2143.exerciseTips:
Use light weights to maintain strict control and prevent injury.
Keep your arms straight but do not lock your elbows tightly.
Maintain a steady, circular motion without jerky stops or pauses.
2143.variations:
Seated Around the World
Plate Front Raise
Dumbbell Shoulder Circles

2144.overview: This exercise targets the pectorals and shoulders muscles, and is suitable for individuals looking to improve overall chest development and strength. It can be used as part of a routine to improve athletic performance and reduce the risk of shoulder injuries.
2144.exerciseTips:
Keep your core engaged to maintain stability.
 Avoid swinging the weight or using momentum.
 Focus on using your chest muscles to lift the weight.
 Use a weight that allows you to complete the desired number of repetitions with proper form.

2186.overview: The ez barbell decline triceps extension is an isolation exercise that targets the triceps, specifically the lateral head. It is suitable for individuals looking to add variety to their tricep workouts and can be performed by those with intermediate to advanced fitness levels. This exercise can help improve overall arm strength and muscle development, and can be used to target specific areas of the triceps.
2186.exerciseTips:
Keep your upper arms still and only move your forearms to isolate the triceps.
Avoid swinging the barbell or using momentum to lift the weight.
Focus on extending your arms fully and squeezing your triceps at the top of the movement.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise.
2186.variations:
Tricep dip
Overhead dumbbell extension
Skull crusher

2187.overview: The barbell reverse close-grip bench press is an exercise that targets the triceps, specifically training the lateral head of the triceps. It is a compound exercise that can be added to a workout routine to improve overall tricep strength and endurance. This exercise is best suited for individuals who want to increase their tricep strength and improve their overall upper arm function.
2187.exerciseTips:
Use a weight that allows you to maintain proper form throughout the exercise
Avoid swinging the barbell or using momentum to lift the weight
Focus on extending your arms rather than contracting your chest
Use a full range of motion, fully extending your arms at the top of the movement
2187.variations:
Barbell close-grip bench press
Dumbbell reverse close-grip bench press

2188.overview: The dumbbell seated triceps extension is an effective isolation exercise for developing all three heads of the triceps, with particular emphasis on the long head. Performing it seated helps stabilize the body, allowing for a focused contraction and a greater range of motion. This exercise is excellent for building triceps size and strength, suitable for all fitness levels.
2188.variations:
single arm dumbbell triceps extension
EZ bar overhead triceps extension
cable overhead triceps extension

2189.overview: The Dumbbell Seated Triceps Extension is a staple isolation exercise that targets the triceps, with a specific emphasis on the long head. By positioning the weight overhead, it stretches the muscle fully for a strong contraction. This movement is suitable for all fitness levels looking to build stronger, more defined arms.
2189.exerciseTips:
Keep your elbows tucked in and pointing toward the ceiling to avoid straining your shoulders.
Move the weight slowly behind your head to feel the stretch.
Avoid flaring your elbows out to the sides as you fatigue.
2189.variations:
Cable Overhead Extension
Lying Triceps Extension
Single Arm Overhead Extension

2202.overview: This exercise utilizes a foam roller to provide a deep stretch for the glutes and hamstrings. It helps improve hip flexibility and can alleviate tightness in the posterior leg muscles.

2203.overview: This exercise uses a roller to engage and stretch the deltoids and pectorals. It's performed while seated and aims to improve shoulder mobility and upper body flexibility.

2204.overview: This core exercise utilizes a foam roller to challenge the abdominal muscles and shoulders. It improves core stability and endurance, making it a good addition for those looking to enhance their midsection strength.

2205.overview: This exercise targets the hips, glutes, and hamstrings using a foam roller. It's designed to improve flexibility and range of motion in the hip joint and surrounding muscles.

2206.overview: This exercise targets the abdominal muscles and hip flexors, using a roller for added challenge and range of motion. It's a good variation for those looking to intensify their core training.

2207.overview: This exercise utilizes a foam roller to stretch the lats and shoulders. It's performed standing with a forward hinge and aims to improve upper body mobility and alleviate tension in the back and shoulder area.

2208.overview: This exercise uses a foam roller to gently stretch the muscles of the back, hamstrings, and glutes. It is beneficial for improving spinal mobility and relieving tension, suitable for most fitness levels.

2271.overview: The left hook is a fundamental boxing technique that targets the deltoids and engages the biceps, triceps, and forearms as secondary muscles. It's suitable for individuals with a basic understanding of boxing stance and technique. This exercise improves punching power, coordination, and overall upper body strength. Boxers and martial artists can benefit from incorporating the left hook into their training routine.
2271.exerciseTips:
Keep your hands up to protect your face and maintain a strong guard.
Rotate your hips to generate power and torque in your punch.
Keep your punches swift and controlled to avoid injury.
2271.variations:
Add a punching bag or pad to practice the left hook with resistance.
Incorporate footwork and movement to simulate a real boxing scenario.

2285.overview: The Lever Pullover is a compound exercise that targets the latissimus dorsi muscles in the back. This exercise is suitable for individuals looking to improve their back strength and width. It is an intermediate-level exercise that requires proper form to avoid injury. By using a leverage machine, individuals can focus on contracting their lats without having to balance heavy weights.
2285.exerciseTips:
Avoid arching your back or using momentum to lift the weight, as this can cause injury.
Keep your core engaged and your arms slightly bent to maintain proper form.
Use a weight that allows you to complete the desired number of repetitions with proper form.
Focus on squeezing your lats at the peak contraction to maximize the exercise's effectiveness.
2285.variations:
Close-Grip Lever Pullover
Wide-Grip Lever Pullover
Incline Lever Pullover

2286.overview: This exercise targets the glutes and hamstrings using a leverage machine with a hip extension movement. It's effective for strengthening the posterior chain and improving hip mobility. Suitable for all fitness levels.

2287.overview: The lever alternate leg press targets the quadriceps and engages the hamstrings and glutes as secondary muscles. It's an intermediate-level exercise suitable for individuals who have experience with leg press machines and are looking to improve their lower body strength. This exercise can help improve athletic performance, enhance muscle balance, and reduce the risk of injury in the knees and hips. Individuals with pre-existing knee or hip injuries should consult with a healthcare professional before attempting this exercise.
2287.exerciseTips:
Focus on extending your legs fully to achieve optimal range of motion.
Avoid using too much weight, which can compromise form and increase the risk of injury.
Keep your core muscles engaged to maintain stability throughout the exercise.
2287.variations:
Use a narrower or wider foot stance to target different muscle groups.
Incorporate pause reps or slow tempos to increase time under tension.

2288.overview: This exercise targets the forearm muscles using a leverage machine's grip handles. It's designed to improve grip strength and forearm endurance. Suitable for all fitness levels.

2289.overview: This exercise targets the calf muscles using a leverage machine. It allows for a full range of motion and controlled resistance, making it effective for building calf size and strength. Suitable for all fitness levels.
2289.variations:
standing calf raise
seated calf raise

2292.overview: The dumbbell rear delt raise (bent‑over lateral raise) targets the posterior deltoids and upper back, improving shoulder stability and posture. It’s appropriate for intermediate lifters wanting balanced shoulder development.
2292.exerciseTips:
Hinge at the hips with a flat back; avoid rounding.
Raise the arms until they’re in line with your torso.
Keep palms facing down or slightly inward for comfort.
Control the descent to maintain tension.
2292.variations:
Perform with elbows slightly bent for a rear‑delt fly variation.
Use a lighter weight and higher reps for endurance.
Do the exercise standing upright for a front‑deltoid emphasis.

2293.overview: The dumbbell standing Zottman preacher curl is a variation of the traditional curl that targets the biceps and forearms. This exercise is suitable for individuals looking to add variety to their arm workout routine. It works the biceps from a different angle, which can help to create a more balanced look. This exercise is best suited for intermediate to advanced lifters due to the need for proper form and control throughout the movement.
2293.exerciseTips:
Keep your core engaged and your back straight throughout the exercise to maintain proper form.
Avoid swinging the dumbbells or using momentum to lift the weight.
Focus on squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
Use a weight that allows you to maintain control throughout the entire range of motion.
2293.variations:
Preacher curls with a barbell or cable machine
Incline dumbbell curls
Hammer curls

2294.overview: This variation places the Zottman Curl on a preacher bench to eliminate momentum and strictly isolate the elbow flexors. It provides an intense stretch in the biceps at the bottom and a strong overload on the forearms during the eccentric phase. It is ideal for bodybuilders focusing on arm aesthetics and maximizing muscle fiber recruitment.
2294.exerciseTips:
Ensure your chest is firmly pressed against the pad to prevent swinging.
Rotate your wrists smoothly at the top to transition into the lowering phase.
Lock your elbows against the pad as the pivot point.
2294.variations:
Preacher Curl
One-Arm Preacher Curl
Spider Curl

2297.overview: This exercise targets the abdominal muscles by utilizing a stability ball for an increased range of motion during the crunch. Holding hands behind the head ensures the neck stays neutral. It's an intermediate exercise for developing the rectus abdominis.

2298.overview: The inverted row on a bench is a versatile bodyweight exercise that targets the upper back and biceps. It helps build pulling strength and improve posture without requiring specialized equipment beyond a stable bench. This variation is accessible for a wide range of fitness levels and can be easily modified.
2298.variations:
Feet elevated inverted row
One-arm inverted row
Inverted row with narrower grip

2300.overview: The inverted row with bent knees is a modified bodyweight exercise designed to strengthen the upper back and biceps. This exercise is excellent for improving posture and building foundational upper body strength.
2300.variations:
Inverted row straight legs
Inverted row on rings
Band-assisted inverted row

2311.overview: This exercise provides a challenging cardio workout by targeting the cardiovascular system. It's suitable for individuals looking to improve their endurance and burn calories. The stepmill component adds an extra challenge, making it a great option for those seeking a more intense workout.
2311.exerciseTips:
Start with a lower resistance and gradually increase as you warm up.
Keep your posture upright and core engaged to maintain balance.
Focus on quick turnover to maintain a steady pace.
2311.variations:
Increase the resistance for a more challenging workout
Add intervals for a HIIT workout

2312.overview: This exercise is a great core strengthener that targets the rectus abdominis and obliques. It involves bringing the elbow to the opposite knee while extending the other leg, improving core stability and coordination. Suitable for beginners.
2312.variations:
lying bicycle crunch
lying knee to elbow

2315.overview: The Lever Rotary Calf is an isolation exercise that targets the calf muscles, specifically the gastrocnemius and soleus. It is suitable for individuals who want to develop stronger, more toned calf muscles, and can be beneficial for athletes who participate in sports that involve running, jumping, or quick changes of direction. This exercise can help improve ankle stability, enhance athletic performance, and reduce the risk of injury. It is also beneficial for individuals who want to develop stronger, more stable ankles.
2315.exerciseTips:
Keep your knees slightly bent throughout the exercise to maintain control and stability.
Focus on pushing through the balls of your feet to raise your heels, rather than relying on momentum.
Avoid letting your heels drop too low, as this can put unnecessary strain on your ankle joints.
2315.variations:
Single-Leg Lever Rotary Calf
Weighted Lever Rotary Calf

2317.overview: The dumbbell seated bent arm lateral raise is a great exercise for targeting the delts and trapezius muscles. It suits individuals who are looking to improve their shoulder strength and stability. This exercise can be modified to suit different fitness levels, making it a great addition to any workout routine. By incorporating this exercise into your routine, you can expect to see improvements in your overall upper body strength.
2317.exerciseTips:
Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability throughout the exercise.
Avoid swinging the dumbbells and focus on controlled, smooth movements.
Start with lighter weights and gradually increase the load as you become more comfortable with the exercise.
2317.variations:
Seated dumbbell lateral raise with straight arms
Standing dumbbell lateral raise

2318.overview: Version 3 offers a similar overhead pressing pattern with adjusted handle positioning for varied deltoid activation. The machine’s stability makes it suitable for beginners progressing to heavier loads. It develops shoulder strength and improves functional overhead movements.

Ensure shoulders are down and back before each rep.
Press the handles in a smooth, controlled arc.
Exhale during the upward phase, inhale on the way down.
Avoid excessive weight that compromises form.
2318.variations:
Switch to a close grip to emphasize the anterior deltoid.
Add a slight pause at lockout for greater muscular activation.
Perform alternating single‑arm presses for core stability.

Keep your elbows stationary at your sides throughout the lift.
Rotate your wrists gradually to hit the muscle from different angles.
Squeeze the biceps hard at the top of the movement.

Reverse Curl
Wide Grip Curl
Zottman Curl

2327.overview: The dumbbell reverse grip row is a variation of the traditional row that targets the upper back, specifically the latissimus dorsi and trapezius muscles. By strengthening the back muscles, individuals can improve their overall athletic performance and reduce the risk of injury.
2327.exerciseTips:
Maintain a straight back and engage your core throughout the exercise to avoid straining your lower back.
Use a weight that allows you to complete the desired number of repetitions with proper form.
Avoid swinging or jerking the dumbbells, focusing on a smooth and controlled movement.

2328.exerciseTips:
Ensure proper foot positioning and body control to maintain balance on the exercise ball.
Avoid letting your hips sag or your back arch, and instead, focus on maintaining a straight line.
Engage your core and use your legs to help with stability.
2328.variations:
Standard push-up: This variation removes the instability of the exercise ball, making it easier to perform.
Wide push-up: This variation increases the difficulty by using a wider grip, which requires increased strength and control in the upper body.
Decline push-up: This variation involves placing the hands on a surface lower than the feet, which will increase the difficulty by engaging the upper body and stabilizing muscles.

2329.overview: This bodyweight exercise targets the obliques and abdominal muscles by focusing on rotational movement. Sitting with knees bent, you twist the torso to bring the elbow towards the opposite knee, enhancing core rotational strength. Suitable for intermediate levels.

2330.overview: The cable lat pulldown with full range of motion effectively targets the latissimus dorsi, improving lat strength and overall back stability. This variation is suitable for individuals with existing shoulder or elbow injuries, as it engages muscles supporting the joints.

Maintain proper posture throughout the movement.
Focus on engaging your lats and avoid swinging the weight.
Adjust the grip width to target the desired muscle group.
2330.variations:
Close-grip variation: Reduce the distance between your hands.
Low-pulley variation: Adjust the cable height to target lower lats.

Keep your back straight and engage your core to maintain balance.
Focus on steady-state pedaling instead of high-intensity intervals if you're a beginner.
2331.variations:
Stairmill Emulation: Adjust the pedals to resemble a stair step and climb the 'staircase' instead of pedaling in a circular motion.
Arm Ergometer: Use the handlebars as an arm ergometer, focusing on rowing movements instead of pedaling.

2333.overview: Hanging straight‑leg raises are a demanding core exercise that targets the rectus abdominis, hip flexors, and stabilizing shoulder muscles. Performing the movement with straight legs increases the lever length, making it more challenging than the bent‑knee variant. Proper form protects the lower back and maximizes abdominal engagement.
2333.exerciseTips:
Keep your torso rigid; avoid arching the lower back as the legs rise.
Focus on pulling with the abs rather than using momentum from the hips.
Breathe out while lifting and inhale on the way down.
If you feel strain in the lower back, bend the knees slightly to reduce lever length.
2333.variations:
Assisted straight‑leg raise with a resistance band
Weighted straight‑leg raise holding a plate between the feet
Captain’s chair straight‑leg raise for added stability

single leg calf press
seated calf press

This exercise can help improve ankle stability, enhance athletic performance, and reduce the risk of injury. It is also beneficial for individuals who want to develop stronger, more stable ankles.
2335.exerciseTips:
Keep your knees in line with your toes throughout the exercise to maintain control and stability.
Focus on extending your ankles to lift your heels, rather than relying on momentum.
Avoid letting your heels drop too low, as this can put unnecessary strain on your ankle joints.

2355.overview: This hanging bent‑knee raise isolates the abdominal muscles and hip flexors while also engaging the shoulders for stabilization. The movement can be progressed by adding weight or increasing range of motion.
2355.exerciseTips:
Avoid swinging; initiate the lift with your core, not momentum.
Keep your shoulders depressed and away from your ears throughout the set.
Exhale on the lift and inhale on the descent for better core activation.
Control the eccentric phase; don’t let your legs drop quickly.
2355.variations:
Assisted bent‑knee raise using a resistance band
Weighted bent‑knee raise holding a medicine ball between the feet

2363.overview: Wide-grip chest dips are an advanced compound exercise primarily targeting the lower chest and triceps. This variation requires significant upper body strength and is suitable for experienced individuals looking to develop pectoral mass and strength.

2368.overview: A unilateral lower body exercise that targets the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings. Performing squats with one leg forward and one back challenges balance and strength individually in each leg. This is an intermediate exercise beneficial for building leg symmetry and power.

2397.overview: The dumbbell scott press is a compound exercise that targets the deltoids and triceps, helping to build overall shoulder strength and development. Keep your core engaged and back straight throughout the exercise to maintain proper form.
Avoid arching your back or using momentum to lift the dumbbells, instead focusing on controlled, smooth movements.
Start with lighter weights and gradually increase the load as you become more comfortable with the exercise.
2397.variations:
Dumbbell Arnold press
Incline dumbbell press

2398.overview: This exercise trains the chest muscles, particularly the triceps and pectorals. It suits individuals who want to improve their upper body strength and mobility in a more comfortable position.

Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability.
Avoid letting your hips sag or your back arch.
Use a slow and controlled tempo to get the most out of the exercise.

2399.overview: The cable seated twist is an isolation exercise that targets the obliques and waist muscles. Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears to maintain stability

2400.overview: The inverse leg curl on a pull-up cable machine is an effective exercise for targeting the hamstrings and glutes. Nordic hamstring curl

2401.overview: Using an arm blaster adds stability and helps to prevent swinging, making it easier to focus on the contraction of the biceps. This exercise targets the biceps and forearms, and is suitable for those who want to improve their arm strength without using heavier weights.

Make sure the arm blaster is set up correctly to prevent injury.
Focus on squeezing your biceps at the top of the movement.
Don't swing the dumbbells or use momentum.

Incline dumbbell curl
Preacher curl

2402.overview: This exercise targets the biceps and forearms, and is ideal for individuals looking to improve their upper arm strength and endurance.

Use a weight that allows you to complete the desired number of repetitions with good form.
Avoid using momentum to curl the dumbbells.
Pause for a brief moment at the top of the curl to maximize contraction.

Neutral grip dumbbell curl
Close grip dumbbell curl
Incline dumbbell hammer curl

2403.overview: Dumbbell alternate bicep curls with an arm blaster target the biceps brachii and brachialis muscles in the upper arms. It's particularly beneficial for individuals who participate in sports that require quick, repetitive movements.
2403.exerciseTips:
Ensure the arm blaster is secure and stable during the movement.
Use a slow and controlled movement to curl the dumbbell.
Avoid swinging the dumbbell and instead focus on engaging your biceps.
2403.variations: Dumbbell bicep curl with arm blaster and alternating hands

2404.variations:
EZ-bar curl (without arm blaster)
Dumbbell arm blaster curl
Cable arm blaster curl

2406.exerciseTips:
Maintain a tight grip throughout the exercise.
Avoid bending your elbows or letting the bar swing.
Focus on contracting your triceps at the bottom of the movement.

2407.overview: The barbell biceps curl is a classic exercise that targets the biceps brachii muscles in the upper arms. It's a great exercise for building overall biceps strength and muscle mass.

Focus on contracting your biceps at the top of the movement.

Keep your upper arms stationary and only move your forearms.

Reverse crunch

It helps improve overall upper body strength and muscle endurance. This exercise is ideal for those who want to build a strong and balanced upper body.
3547.exerciseTips:
Maintain proper form and avoid arching your back.
Focus on controlled movements and proper form.
Use a weight that allows you to complete the full range of motion.
Start with lighter weights and gradually increase as you build strength and endurance.
3547.variations:
Dumbbell curl to shoulder press standing
Barbell curl to shoulder press
Incline dumbbell curl to shoulder press

3548.overview: The single arm overhead carry is a highly effective functional exercise that challenges core stability, shoulder strength, and balance. It helps improve overall body awareness and resilience, making it excellent for athletes and those seeking to enhance functional strength. Suitable for intermediate to advanced users, it builds strong, stable shoulders and a robust core.
3548.variations:
two-arm overhead carry
farmer's walk
single arm rack carry

3552.overview: This is a plyometric exercise designed to improve foot speed, agility, and cardiovascular endurance. It involves rapidly tapping the balls of your feet on the ground, mimicking a running motion, and is excellent for athletes or anyone looking to enhance coordination.
3552.variations:
Incorporate high knees.
Alternate with butt kicks.

3560.overview: This compound movement combines a hammer curl with an overhead press to target the biceps, forearms, and shoulders simultaneously. It is excellent for improving upper-body strength and muscular endurance. The alternating nature helps maintain core stability and balance throughout the set.
3560.exerciseTips:
Keep your core tight to prevent swaying or arching your back during the press.
Do not use momentum to swing the dumbbells up; focus on controlled muscle contractions.
Maintain a slight bend in your knees to help absorb pressure and improve stability.
3560.variations:
Alternating Hammer Curl
Seated Dumbbell Press
Thrusters

3561.overview: The glute bridge march is a bodyweight exercise that targets the glutes and hamstrings, making it an excellent option for individuals looking to improve their lower body strength and overall athletic performance. This exercise suits beginners to intermediate individuals who are looking to improve their hip and glute strength. By engaging the glutes and maintaining proper form, individuals can effectively work their glutes and hamstrings while minimizing the risk of injury. The glute bridge march is a versatile exercise that can be incorporated into a variety of workout routines, from strength training to cardio and flexibility exercises.
3561.exerciseTips:
Keep your core engaged and your hips lifted throughout the movement to maintain proper form and engage the correct muscles.
Avoid arching your back or using momentum to lift your hips, as this can put unnecessary strain on your lower back.
Start with a slower pace and gradually increase the speed as you become more comfortable with the exercise.
3561.variations:
Glute bridge march with leg lift: Lift one leg off the ground and hold it for a few seconds before lowering it back down and repeating with the other leg.
Glute bridge march with pause: Hold the bridge position for a few seconds before continuing with the march.

3562.overview: Performing the glute bridge with the upper back supported on a bench increases the range of motion and emphasizes hip extension. Loading the hips with a barbell adds significant resistance, making this an effective move for strengthening the glutes and hamstrings. It is suitable for beginners who have mastered the basic bridge.
3562.exerciseTips:
Keep the shoulders firmly on the bench to avoid slipping.
Drive through the heels and keep the knees tracking over the feet.
Avoid overextending the lower back; stop when hips are in line with the shoulders.
Engage the core throughout to maintain spinal stability.
3562.variations:
Single‑leg bridge on bench for unilateral focus
Barbell hip thrust with feet on the floor and shoulders on bench
Glute bridge on bench using a resistance band for added tension

3563.overview: The one‑arm pulldown isolates the latissimus dorsi while also engaging the biceps and forearms for grip. Constant cable tension ensures a smooth range of motion, making it an effective intermediate exercise for building back width.
3563.exerciseTips:
Keep your torso upright; avoid leaning back to cheat the movement.
Pull with the elbow, not the forearm, to maximize lat activation.
Avoid excessive swinging; perform the motion in a controlled manner.
Keep the shoulder down and away from the ear throughout the set.
3563.variations:
High‑pulley single‑hand lat pulldown with a rope attachment
Alternating single‑arm pulldown using a straight bar
Single‑arm pulldown performed from a kneeling position for core engagement

3582.overview: A dynamic exercise that combines the benefits of lunges with explosive power from jumping. It primarily targets the quadriceps, glutes, and hamstrings, while also improving cardiovascular fitness and agility. Suitable for intermediate to advanced individuals.
3582.variations:
walking lunge with jump
reverse lunge with jump

3635.overview: This exercise targets the glutes and quadriceps, and is a great option for those looking to improve their balance and coordination. It's an intermediate-level exercise that suits those who have a good understanding of proper lunge form and can maintain balance on one leg. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand.
3635.exerciseTips:
Keep your back straight and core engaged throughout the exercise.
Take small steps forward to ensure control and balance.
Focus on lower body movement, not upper body movement.
3635.variations:
Single-leg dumbbell lunges
Dumbbell walking lunges

3636.overview: The high knee against wall is a dynamic cardiovascular exercise that improves agility, leg drive, and coordination. It's an excellent choice for a warm-up or as part of a conditioning routine to boost heart rate and activate the lower body.
3636.variations:
High knee run in place
Marching high knees
Butt kicks

3637.overview: The wheel run is a challenging cardiovascular exercise that engages your entire core and upper body. It's suitable for individuals looking to improve their endurance and build functional strength, particularly in the abdominal and back muscles.
3637.variations:
tuck wheel run
single leg wheel run
wheel run with leg lift

3638.overview: The push-to-run is a high-intensity hybrid exercise that combines a push-up with mountain climbers. It builds upper body strength while simultaneously elevating the heart rate for cardiovascular benefits. This full-body movement is excellent for metabolic conditioning and improving coordination.
3638.exerciseTips:
Keep your hips low during the mountain climber portion to engage the core.
Explosively switch legs to maximize the cardio benefit.
Do not let your lower back sag; maintain a straight line.
Land lightly on the balls of your feet to reduce impact.
3638.variations:
Slow mountain climbers
Burpee
Push-up to pike

3639.overview: The bent knee lying twist primarily targets the obliques and hip flexors, making it an excellent exercise for individuals looking to improve their rotational strength and stability. This exercise is ideal for individuals of all fitness levels and can be modified to suit various training goals. By engaging the core and performing the twist, individuals can enhance their overall core strength and reduce the risk of injury.
3639.exerciseTips:
Avoid using momentum to twist your torso.
Focus on engaging your core muscles throughout the entire movement.
Slow and controlled movements are essential for this exercise.
3639.variations:
Weighted knee twist (using dumbbells or a weight plate)
Alternating side knee twist (alternating sides with each rep)
Resistance band rotational twist (using a resistance band for added resistance)

3640.overview: The knee touch crunch is an isolation exercise that trains the abs, targeting the rectus abdominis muscle. It is suitable for individuals looking to improve their core strength and athletic performance. This exercise requires proper form and technique to avoid injury, making it an intermediate-level exercise. It also engages the hip flexors, making it a great option for those looking to work multiple muscle groups at once.
3640.exerciseTips:
Keep your lower back pressed into the ground throughout the exercise to maintain proper form and avoid injury.
Use a slow and controlled motion to lift and lower your torso, avoiding momentum and bounce.
Avoid using your hip flexors to lift your torso, instead focusing on engaging your abs to generate force.
Focus on squeezing your abs at the top of the movement to fully engage your core muscles.
3640.variations:
Russian twist: Perform the exercise with a weight or medicine ball, twisting your torso from side to side to engage your obliques.
Leg raise crunch: Perform the exercise with your legs straight, lifting them off the ground and towards the ceiling to engage your lower abs.

3641.overview: This exercise combines a kneeling stance with an overhead swing, engaging the shoulders, triceps, and core. It's suitable for intermediate individuals looking to improve explosive power and upper body strength.

3642.overview: The weighted stretch lunge targets the glutes, quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It suits intermediate to advanced lifters looking to build strength and flexibility in their lower body.
3642.exerciseTips:
Keep your front knee behind your toes.
Lower yourself down slowly and control the movement.
Avoid leaning forward or arching your back.
3642.variations:
bodyweight lunge
walking lunge
side lunge

3643.overview: This exercise targets the glutes, with secondary emphasis on the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It is suitable for intermediate individuals looking to build strength and mobility in their lower body.
3643.exerciseTips:
Keep your back straight and core engaged to maintain stability and control throughout the movement.
Avoid letting your knee extend past your toes, as this can put unnecessary strain on your joints.
Focus on pushing through your heel to return to the starting position, rather than using your back or momentum.
3643.variations:
bodyweight cossack squats
cossack squats with a shorter range of motion

3644.overview: This dynamic exercise combines a weighted lunge with an explosive swing, targeting the lower body and shoulders simultaneously. It's great for intermediate to advanced trainees aiming to improve coordination and power.

3645.overview: This variation of the glute bridge targets the glutes and hamstrings of the planted leg while improving balance and stability. Extending the opposite leg increases the challenge and isolates the working side.
3645.variations:
with foot elevated
with resistance band around knees

3655.overview: This exercise is a dynamic cardio workout that targets the cardiovascular system while engaging the quadriceps. It's suitable for individuals looking to improve their cardiovascular endurance and leg strength. The high knees component adds an extra challenge to the traditional lunge, making it a great option for those seeking a more intense workout.
3655.exerciseTips:
Keep your core engaged to maintain balance and stability.
Land softly on the balls of your feet to reduce impact on your joints.
Focus on quick turnover to maintain a steady pace.
3655.variations:
Add a resistance band for added challenge
Increase the height of your knee lift

3656.overview: This is a cardiovascular exercise that focuses on maintaining a high intensity with short, quick steps. It's effective for improving cardiovascular health and endurance.

3662.overview: This dynamic exercise transitions from a pike position to a cobra pose, engaging the shoulders, chest, and core. It improves flexibility, upper body strength, and mobility.
3662.exerciseTips:
Move smoothly and continuously without pausing too long.
Keep your elbows close to your body during the lowering phase.
Keep your core tight to prevent your hips from sagging.
3662.variations:
Pike push-up
Cobra stretch
Up dog to down dog

3663.overview: This exercise engages the glutes and hamstrings while strengthening the core and shoulders. It's performed in a reverse plank position with alternating leg lifts, making it a good option for improving stability and lower body control.

3664.overview: This is an advanced compound exercise that combines core stability from a side plank with upper back and shoulder engagement from a rear fly. It effectively strengthens the obliques, shoulders, and upper back, improving rotational stability and posterior chain strength. Ideal for advanced individuals seeking a challenging full-body integration.
3664.variations:
side plank without fly
bent-over dumbbell rear fly
cable rear fly

3665.overview: Also known as a plank up-down or walkout, this dynamic exercise transitions between a high plank and a forearm plank. It challenges the core, shoulders, and triceps while requiring significant stability to prevent swaying. It is an effective progression from the standard static plank for improving shoulder endurance and core strength.
3665.exerciseTips:
Keep your hips parallel to the floor and avoid rocking or swaying during the transition.
Move one arm at a time deliberately to maintain balance.
Engage your core tightly to protect your lower back.
Keep your gaze down to maintain a neutral neck position.
3665.variations:
Plank shoulder taps
Side plank up-down
Knee plank up-down

3666.overview: This exercise provides an effective cardio workout by targeting the cardiovascular system. It's suitable for individuals looking to improve their endurance and burn calories. The incline component adds an extra challenge, making it a great option for those seeking a more intense workout.
3666.exerciseTips:
Start with a lower incline and gradually increase as you warm up.
Keep your posture upright and core engaged to maintain balance.
Stay hydrated throughout your workout.
3666.variations:
Increase the incline for a more challenging workout
Add intervals for a HIIT workout

3667.overview: This exercise targets the adductor muscles (inner thigh) while lying on your side. It helps improve inner thigh strength and flexibility, complementing exercises that focus on the outer hip and glutes.
3667.variations:
with ankle weight
using a resistance band

3669.overview: The standing archer is an exercise that targets the upper back, shoulders, and biceps. It requires a good amount of strength, control, and coordination. This exercise is best suited for intermediate athletes.
3669.exerciseTips:
Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain control and stability.
Focus on slow and controlled movements to avoid injury.
Start with a shorter range of motion and gradually increase as you build strength and control.
3669.variations:
Seated archer: Perform the exercise while seated on a chair or bench to reduce the strain on your lower back.
Modified archer: Use a lighter range of motion or slower tempo to make the exercise more manageable.

3670.overview: This exercise targets the abdominal muscles, with secondary emphasis on the hip flexors and lower back. It is suitable for intermediate individuals looking to build strength and definition in their core.
3670.exerciseTips:
Keep your core engaged to maintain stability and control throughout the movement.
Avoid using momentum or jerking to lift your upper body.
Focus on using your abdominal muscles to control the movement, rather than relying on the decline of the bench.
3670.variations:
unweighted decline sit-ups
decline sit-ups on a flat bench

3671.overview: This is a dynamic cardio exercise that mimics the side-to-side motion of skiing. It engages the legs and glutes while providing an excellent cardiovascular workout.

3672.overview: The back and forth step is a cardiovascular exercise that targets the quadriceps and secondary muscle groups such as the hamstrings, glutes, and calf muscles. This exercise is ideal for those seeking to improve their agility, coordination, and endurance. It is particularly useful for athletes participating in sports that involve rapid changes in direction, such as tennis or basketball.
3672.exerciseTips:
Maintain a steady pace and avoid slowing down as you continue.
Keep your posture upright and engage your core throughout the exercise.
Focus on quick, light steps.
Avoid overextending your knees or using momentum to propel yourself forward.

3679.overview: This variation of the sit-up places emphasis on the abdominal muscles by altering the arm position. It helps in building core strength and stability.

3697.overview: This exercise targets the rear deltoids by retracting the shoulder blades, engaging the trapezius to pull the cable. It suits individuals who struggle with traditional row exercises.

Maintain a stable core throughout the exercise
Use your shoulder blades to pull the cable, not just your arms
Kneel on a mat or towel for added comfort
3697.variations: Using a heavier cable resistance for increased challenge

3698.overview: The inchworm v. 2 is a variation of the traditional inchworm exercise. It targets the muscles in the waist, specifically the abs and shoulders, and is a dynamic exercise that involves movement and requires strength, control, and endurance. This exercise is suitable for individuals of all fitness levels, including beginners and advanced athletes. By incorporating inchworm v. 2 into your workout routine, you can improve your overall core strength and increase your flexibility.
3698.exerciseTips:
Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise to maintain stability.
Use a slow and controlled motion when walking your hands forward and your feet backward.
Focus on keeping your body in a straight line from head to toe.
3698.variations:
Modified inchworm v. 2
Weighted inchworm v. 2

3699.overview: This exercise targets your abs and obliques by engaging your core to stabilize your body while alternating arm reaches. It's a great bodyweight exercise for improving core strength and shoulder stability, suitable for most fitness levels.

3758.overview: The standing chest press on a lever machine works the pectorals, shoulders, and triceps in a standing, functional position. The guided path reduces the need for a spotter, making it beginner‑friendly. It enhances upper‑body pushing strength and core stability.

Keep shoulders down and back, avoiding elevation.
Press the handles forward while maintaining a slight bend in the elbows.
Exhale during the press, inhale while returning.
Engage the core to keep the torso stable throughout.
3758.variations:

Use a neutral grip for reduced shoulder stress.
Perform the press with a staggered stance for increased core engagement.

3759.overview: The lever seated good morning strengthens the hamstrings, glutes, and lower back while providing spinal support via the machine. This variation reduces the need for heavy free weights, making it accessible to beginners and those with limited flexibility. It improves posterior chain strength essential for lifting and athletic performance.
3759.exerciseTips:
Keep a neutral spine and avoid rounding the lower back.
Push the hips back rather than bending at the waist.
Engage the core throughout to protect the spine.
Control the descent to maintain tension in the hamstrings.
3759.variations:
Increase the range of motion by moving the seat lower for a deeper hinge.
Add a pause at the bottom of the movement to increase glute activation.
Perform the movement with the feet in a wider stance to emphasize the inner hamstrings.

3760.overview: Version 2 of the lever seated crunch adds hip‑flexor engagement, making it a compound core exercise that works both the obliques and hip flexors. The machine support allows for a safe, controlled contraction, suitable for beginner to intermediate lifters. This movement improves core strength and pelvic stability.
3760.exerciseTips:
Maintain a slight bend in the knees to protect the joints.
Contract the abs first before flexing at the hips.
Keep the movement smooth; avoid jerking the lever.
Fully extend the hips at the bottom to feel a stretch in the hip flexors.
3760.variations:
Perform the crunch with a reverse grip to shift emphasis to the lower abs.
Add a pause at the top for increased isometric hold.
Use a narrower foot placement to increase hip‑flexor activation.

3769.overview: The curtsey squat exercise targets the glutes, quadriceps, hamstrings, and calves. It's an excellent exercise for those with strength imbalances between the legs as it forces you to engage your core and stabilizers.
3769.exerciseTips:
Keep your back straight and your core engaged to maintain balance.
Focus on lowering your weight gradually, avoiding bouncy movements.
3769.variations:
Sumo Squat Curtsey: Stand wider than shoulder-width apart with your feet and take a step sideways instead of diagonally.
Side Step Curtsey: Take a step to one side instead of diagonally, mimicking a curtsey movement.

3785.overview: The incline push-up on a box is a variation of the traditional push-up that targets the chest, triceps, and shoulders, helping to improve upper body strength and endurance. It is suitable for individuals of all fitness levels, as the height of the box can be adjusted to modify the difficulty of the exercise. By performing a push-up on a box, individuals can reduce the challenge to their chest muscles and focus on targeting their triceps and shoulders. This exercise is also effective for improving overall upper body strength and stability.
3785.exerciseTips:
Keep your core engaged and your body aligned throughout the exercise to maintain proper form and prevent straining your lower back.
Focus on keeping your elbows close to your body as you lower and raise your chest to target the triceps effectively.
Avoid letting your hips sag or your back arch, as this can put unnecessary strain on your spine.
3785.variations:
Decline push-up: Perform the exercise with your hands on a lower surface to increase the challenge to your chest muscles.
Diamond push-up: Place your hands closer together to increase the challenge to your triceps.

3888.overview: The dumbbell one arm snatch is a compound exercise that primarily targets the glutes and hamstrings. It's a great exercise for those looking to improve their power and coordination. This exercise suits individuals with a good level of strength and mobility, particularly in their hips and legs.
3888.exerciseTips:
Keep your back straight and chest up throughout the movement.
Use your hips and legs to generate power for the lift.
Keep the dumbbell close to your body throughout the movement.
3888.variations:
Two-arm snatch
Snatch with a deficit (e.g., on a step or bench)

5201.overview: The Dumbbell Waiter Biceps Curl is a fundamental isolation exercise that targets the biceps brachii to build arm size and strength. It is a staple movement for beginners and advanced lifters alike, focusing on the elbow flexion function of the biceps. This exercise helps develop overall upper body aesthetics and pulling power.
5201.exerciseTips:
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides to prevent swinging and ensure bicep isolation.
Do not use momentum; if you have to swing your hips, the weight is too heavy.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement for a peak contraction.
5201.variations:
Hammer Curl
Concentration Curl
Incline Dumbbell Curl

0013.overview: This exercise targets the hip flexors and is suitable for those looking to increase their core strength and mobility. It involves lifting the legs off the ground and throwing them down, making it a great addition to your workout routine. However, please note that it can be challenging and may require assistance. Suitable for intermediate to advanced individuals.
0013.exerciseTips:
Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Use your glutes to assist with the movement.
Slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.

0014.overview: This exercise targets the obliques and is suitable for those looking to improve their core rotation and stability. It involves holding a medicine ball and twisting your torso, making it a great addition to your workout routine. However, please note that it can be challenging and may require assistance. Suitable for intermediate to advanced individuals.
0014.exerciseTips:
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Use your obliques to assist with the movement.
Slowly rotate your torso without jerking the medicine ball.

0015.overview: This exercise targets the lats and is suitable for those looking to improve their back strength and endurance. It involves hanging from a lever machine and pulling up towards the bars, making it a great addition to your workout routine. However, please note that it can be challenging and may require assistance. Suitable for intermediate to advanced individuals.
0015.exerciseTips:
Keep your elbows close to your body throughout the exercise.
Use your back muscles to assist with the movement.
Slowly lower your body back down to the starting position.

0016.overview: This exercise targets the hamstrings and is suitable for those looking to improve their lower leg strength and flexibility. It involves lying face down and lifting your legs towards your glutes, making it a great addition to your workout routine. However, please note that it can be challenging and may require assistance. Suitable for intermediate to advanced individuals.
0016.exerciseTips:
Keep your knees straight throughout the exercise.
Use your glutes to assist with the movement.
Slowly lower your legs back down to the starting position.

0001.overview: The 3/4 sit-up targets the abdominal muscles and hip flexors while limiting strain on the lower back. It is a good progression from a partial sit-up for beginners who want to build core strength. This variation is useful for those who experience discomfort with full sit-ups.
0001.exerciseTips:
Keep your neck in line with your spine and avoid pulling on your head with your hands.
Focus on engaging the abdominal muscles rather than using momentum.
Breathe out on the upward phase and inhale on the way down.
Maintain a controlled tempo to prevent lower‑back arching.
0001.variations:
Full sit‑up for greater range of motion
Weighted sit‑up holding a plate or dumbbell
Decline sit‑up on an angled bench

0002.overview: The 45° side bend works the oblique muscles and improves lateral spinal flexibility. It is a low‑impact movement suitable for beginners and for anyone looking to enhance core stability. Proper form helps avoid unnecessary strain on the lower back.
0002.exerciseTips:
Keep your spine neutral; avoid rounding your back as you bend.
Breathe out on the side‑bending phase and inhale as you return to center.
Initiate the movement from the waist, not from the shoulders.
Maintain a slight bend in the supporting knee to reduce joint stress.
0002.variations:
Standing cable side pull with a band for added resistance
Seated side bend while sitting on a bench
Side plank with a reach‑under for an advanced variation

0003.overview: The air bike is a dynamic core exercise that combines a bicycle motion with an anti‑rotation element, targeting the hip flexors, rectus abdominis, and obliques. It also provides a cardiovascular challenge, making it ideal for intermediate‑level workouts. Proper technique ensures spinal safety while maximizing abdominal activation.
0003.exerciseTips:
Press your lower back into the floor throughout the movement to protect the spine.
Keep the motion controlled; avoid using momentum to swing the legs.
Exhale as you bring the elbow to the knee and inhale on the return.
Maintain a steady tempo rather than racing through reps.
0003.variations:
Bicycle crunch without the leg extension for a beginner version
Weighted air bike holding a light plate for added resistance
Standing air bike using a suspended leg strap for a full‑body challenge

0006.overview: Alternate heel touchers engage the obliques and rectus abdominis through a side‑to‑side reaching motion while keeping the core stable. This body‑weight exercise is beginner‑friendly and effective for building rotational strength. It also improves coordination between the upper and lower body.
0006.exerciseTips:
Keep your neck neutral; avoid pulling on your head with your hands.
Perform the movement slowly to maximize muscle tension rather than using momentum.
Drive the elbow toward the heel by rotating through the torso, not just moving the arm.
Exhale on the reaching phase and inhale on the return.
0006.variations:
Standing heel touchers for a functional variation
Weighted heel touchers holding a light plate or medicine ball
Russian twist with a pause at the side for increased time under tension

0007.overview: Alternate lateral pulldowns develop the latissimus dorsi, biceps, and supporting shoulder muscles while allowing each side to work independently. Using a cable machine, the movement mimics a rowing action and is appropriate for intermediate trainees seeking balanced back development. Maintaining a stable torso ensures maximal fiber recruitment and reduces injury risk.
0007.exerciseTips:
Keep your torso upright; avoid excessive leaning backwards during the pull.
Engage your lats by pulling from the elbows, not just the hands.
Control the eccentric phase; don’t let the weight snap back.
Breathe out while pulling and inhale while returning the weight.
0007.variations:
Single‑arm lateral pulldown for unilateral focus
Underhand‑grip pulldown to emphasize the lower lats
Resistance‑band lateral pulldown for a portable alternative

0009.overview: The assisted chest dip on a leverage machine allows beginners to develop pectoral, triceps, and front‑deltoid strength with reduced body weight load. Kneeling on the pad provides support while still requiring core stability, making it an effective progression toward full dips. Maintaining proper elbow position protects the shoulder joint.

Keep your elbows close to your body to target the chest more than the shoulders.
Do not let the shoulders roll forward; keep them down and back throughout the movement.
Descend only as far as comfortable; a shallow dip is safer for beginners.
Engage your core to stabilize the torso and prevent excessive forward lean.
0009.variations:
Assisted dip with a resistance band for added support
Bench dip using a stable bench for a home‑friendly version
Weighted dip using a dip belt once strength improves

0011.overview: Assisted hanging knee raises develop core strength while the machine or band reduces the portion of body weight you must lift. This makes the exercise suitable for beginners who want to progress toward full hanging leg raises. Proper scapular depression keeps the shoulders stable during the movement.
0011.exerciseTips:
Maintain a slight bend in the elbows to keep the shoulders relaxed.
Avoid swinging; initiate the lift with your core, not momentum.
Breathe out while lifting the knees and inhale on the way down.
Keep your shoulders depressed to protect the rotator cuff.
0011.variations:
Straight‑leg assisted raise for an added challenge
Weighted assisted raise holding a small plate between the feet
Captain’s chair knee raise as an alternative equipment option

0010.overview: This explosive variation adds a dynamic throw‑down to the assisted hanging knee raise, increasing power and recruiting the hip flexors, core, and lower‑body muscles. The movement is suitable for intermediate trainees aiming to improve athletic explosiveness while still receiving assistance to control body weight. Proper landing technique is essential to protect the spine and shoulders.
0010.exerciseTips:
Control the landing; bend the knees slightly to absorb impact and protect the lower back.
Keep your core braced throughout the explosive phase to avoid excessive swinging.
Exhale sharply on the throw‑down and inhale as you reset the position.
Maintain scapular depression to keep the shoulders stable during rapid movement.
0010.variations:
Toe‑to‑bar throw‑down for a full‑body version
Weighted throw‑down holding a medicine ball between the feet
Assisted version using a resistance band to reduce load

0012.overview: This exercise combines a straight‑leg raise with a lateral throw, engaging the rectus abdominis, obliques, and hip flexors while adding an explosive element for power development. Controlling the descent protects the lower back and maintains tension in the core muscles.

Press your lower back into the floor to prevent arching as the legs lift.
Move slowly during the side‑lower phase; a controlled motion maximizes oblique activation.
Keep your legs together and avoid letting them drift apart during the throw.
Exhale on the lift and inhale on the lateral throw for better core stability.

Band‑resisted lateral throw to increase difficulty
Side‑plank leg raise as an alternative unilateral core challenge

0017.overview: The assisted pull-up is a compound exercise that targets the back muscles, improving strength and control. This exercise is suitable for individuals who need assistance to perform a traditional pull-up, including those returning from injury or new to strength training.
0017.exerciseTips:
Focus on squeezing your lats at the top of the movement.
Keep your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Don't swing or jerk the weight.

0018.overview: This exercise is great for strengthening your triceps. It's an excellent option for those who struggle with traditional triceps extensions.

0018.variations: Using a resistance band instead of a towel

0019.overview: This exercise is great for strengthening your triceps. It's an excellent option for those who struggle with traditional triceps dips.
0019.exerciseTips: Make sure to keep your back straight and engage your core throughout the exercise.
0019.variations: Increasing the weight to make the exercise more challenging

0020.overview: This exercise targets the quads, training them to maintain balance and stability. It's suitable for individuals looking to improve their balance and proprioception.
0020.exerciseTips:
Keep your knees slightly bent to reduce the risk of falling.
Engage your core to maintain stability.
Slowly shift your weight to avoid loss of balance.
0020.variations:
Single-leg balance
Balance board with eyes closed
Balance board on a foam pad

0968.overview: This exercise targets the biceps, training them to contract and flex. It's suitable for individuals looking to build stronger arms.

0376.overview: The dumbbell raise (lateral raise) isolates the medial deltoids, helping to broaden the shoulders. It’s a beginner‑friendly exercise that can be performed with light weights for shoulder definition.

Keep a slight bend in the elbows to reduce joint stress.
Avoid using momentum; raise the weights slowly.
Maintain a tight core to prevent swaying.

Perform seated to eliminate lower‑body assistance.
Use cables for constant tension.

0377.overview: The dumbbell rear delt row combines a rowing motion with rear‑deltoid activation, strengthening the upper back and shoulders. It’s an intermediate exercise beneficial for posture improvement.

Pull the dumbbells toward the ribs, squeezing the shoulder blades.
Maintain elbows close to the body to emphasize the rear delts.
Avoid shrugging shoulders during the lift.

Perform with one arm at a time for unilateral control.
Swap to a barbell for a wider grip row.

0378.overview: The dumbbell rear fly isolates the posterior deltoids and rhomboids, helping to improve shoulder external rotation and upper‑back strength. Suitable for beginners to intermediate lifters.
0378.exerciseTips:

Lead with the elbows rather than the hands.
Keep the torso stable; avoid rocking.
Exhale as you lift the weights.

Use cables for continuous tension.
Increase the angle of torso inclination to vary the stress.

0380.overview: The dumbbell rear lateral raise (bent‑over) targets the rear delts and upper traps, promoting balanced shoulder development. It’s a beginner‑friendly movement that can be done with light dumbbells.

Raise arms to shoulder height with palms facing each other.
Control both the upward and downward phases.
Keep shoulders down away from ears.

Use a single arm to focus on each side individually.
Do the movement seated to eliminate momentum.

0379.overview: The rear lateral raise with head support offers a stable position for focusing on posterior deltoid activation, reducing strain on the neck. Good for beginners seeking shoulder isolation.

Lift the arms in a controlled arc, avoiding jerky motions.

Breathe out on the lift and inhale on the return.

Use lighter weights and higher reps for endurance.

Engage the core throughout the movement.

0383.overview: The dumbbell reverse fly targets the rear deltoids, trapezius, and rhomboids, enhancing shoulder stability and posture. It’s a beginner movement that can be performed with light weights for higher reps.

0606.overview: The lever t-bar row is a machine-based exercise that targets the upper back muscles, including the latissimus dorsi and trapezius. 0606.exerciseTips:
Focus on using your back muscles to pull the handles towards your torso, and avoid swinging your body or using momentum.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you pull the handles, and avoid letting them flare out to the sides.
Use a full range of motion by pulling the handles all the way towards your torso, and then releasing them back to the starting position.
0606.variations:

It is suitable for those who require a low-impact alternative to free weight extensions, such as those with shoulder or elbow injuries. This exercise is a great addition to a triceps day workout routine.
0607.exerciseTips:
Focus on extending your arms fully at the starting position, and avoid using momentum to lift the handles.
Keep your upper arms still throughout the movement, and avoid swinging your body or using momentum.
Use a full range of motion by lowering the handles all the way towards your forehead, and then pushing them back up to the starting position.
0607.variations: Close-grip lever triceps extension: Grasp the handles closer than shoulder-width apart to target the lateral head of the triceps.

0609.overview: The London Bridge is a bodyweight exercise that targets the upper back muscles, including the latissimus dorsi and trapezius. It is suitable for building strength and endurance in a variety of individuals. This exercise is a great addition to a back day workout routine.
0609.exerciseTips:
Focus on using your back muscles to pull the rope towards your body, and avoid swinging your body or using momentum.
Keep your elbows close to your body as you pull the rope, and avoid letting them flare out to the sides.
Use a full range of motion by pulling the rope all the way towards your body, and then releasing it back to the starting position.

0628.overview: Monster walk is a bodyweight exercise that targets the glutes and hamstrings while engaging the core. Make sure to keep the tension on the resistance band throughout the movement.
Keep your back straight and your core engaged throughout the exercise.
Avoid using momentum or letting your knees sag.

Keep your arms straight and use your legs to propel yourself.

Depth jump mountain climber

0631.overview: Muscle up is a compound exercise that targets the lats, biceps, and chest while engaging the core. Make sure to engage your core and keep your body straight throughout the movement.
Avoid lifting your hips or letting your back arch.
Use your lats to pull yourself up and your chest to support your body.

Kipping muscle up
Corkscrew muscle up

0595.overview: This lever seated crunch using the chest pad isolates the rectus abdominis and obliques while offering a stable support surface. It suits beginners and intermediate trainees looking for a controlled core exercise. Adjusting the chest pad changes the angle of the movement, allowing you to emphasize different parts of the abdominal wall.
0595.exerciseTips:
Ensure the chest pad is aligned with the mid‑sternum for proper leverage.
Drive the movement with your abs, keeping shoulders relaxed.
Breathe out during the crunch and inhale as you return.
Avoid using momentum; keep the motion smooth.
0595.variations:
Increase the angle of the chest pad to perform an incline crunch.
Add a slight lateral tilt to target the side obliques.
Combine with a slow 3‑second eccentric for greater time under tension.

0596.overview: The lever seated fly isolates the pectoral muscles and front deltoids, offering a safe alternative to free‑weight flyes. The machine guides the movement, reducing stress on the shoulder joints, making it suitable for beginners and rehab populations. It enhances chest development and shoulder stability.
0596.exerciseTips:
Keep a slight bend in the elbows throughout to protect the joint.
Lead the movement with the chest, not the forearms.
Exhale as you bring the handles together, inhale on the return.
Avoid letting the weights pull your arms too far back, which can strain the shoulders.
0596.variations:
Adjust the seat height to target different portions of the pecs.
Perform a slight hug motion by bringing the handles together more closely.
Use a slower eccentric phase for increased muscle time under tension.

0597.overview: This exercise isolates the hip abductors, primarily the gluteus medius, while also engaging the glutes and hamstrings. The seated lever setup provides stability, suitable for beginners and rehabilitation protocols. Strengthening abductors improves hip stability and lateral movement control.
0597.exerciseTips:
Keep a slight bend in the knees to reduce joint stress.
Focus on moving the leg laterally using the hip, not the knees.
Avoid swinging the torso; keep upper body stable.
Exhale while pushing apart, inhale as you return.
0597.variations:
Perform a single‑leg abduction for unilateral focus.
Add a pause at the end of the movement for isometric strength.
Increase the weight gradually to challenge the muscles.

0598.overview: The lever seated hip adduction targets the inner thigh muscles (adductors) while also recruiting the hamstrings and glutes. The machine offers a controlled environment, ideal for beginners and those recovering from hip injuries. Regular training enhances medial thigh strength and overall leg stability.
0598.exerciseTips:
Keep the torso upright and avoid leaning forward.
Drive the movement with the thigh muscles, not momentum.
Exhale as you bring the legs together, inhale as you separate.
Maintain a smooth tempo; avoid rapid snapping.
0598.variations:
Use a slower eccentric phase to increase muscle activation.
Add a brief hold at maximum contraction.
Perform unilateral adduction for balance development.

0599.overview: The seated leg curl on a lever machine isolates the hamstrings and provides secondary activation of the calves. The seated position reduces lower back strain, making it suitable for beginners and those with back concerns. It improves knee flexor strength and muscle balance.
0599.exerciseTips:
Adjust the lever pad just above the ankle to align with the joint.
Keep hips pressed against the backrest to isolate hamstrings.
Exhale while curling, inhale on the return.
Avoid using momentum; lift in a controlled manner.
0599.variations:
Perform a double‑leg curl with a slower tempo.
Do single‑leg curls to address side imbalances.
Add a pause at the top for increased time under tension.

0600.overview: Combining a leg raise with a torso crunch, this movement works the lower abs, hip flexors, and core stabilizers. The lever machine provides support, allowing beginners to perform the exercise safely. It enhances abdominal strength and hip flexor flexibility.
0600.exerciseTips:
Keep the lower back lightly pressed against the backrest.
Lead the motion with the abs, not by swinging the legs.
Exhale during the crunch and leg raise, inhale on the return.
Maintain a controlled tempo to avoid momentum.
0600.variations:
Perform the movement with straight legs for greater hip‑flexor demand.
Add a pause at the top for an isometric hold.
Use a partial range to focus on the lower abdominal contraction.

0602.overview: The seated reverse fly targets the posterior deltoids, trapezius, and rhomboids, promoting shoulder stability and posture. The lever machine guides the movement, suitable for beginners and those with shoulder issues. It balances front‑deltoid dominance from pressing exercises.
0602.exerciseTips:
Keep shoulders down and back throughout the lift.
Lead the motion with the elbows, not the hands.
Exhale while pulling the handles back, inhale on the return.
Avoid using excessive weight that compromises form.
0602.variations:
Perform the reverse fly with a slight hinge forward for increased rear‑deltoid emphasis.
Do a single‑arm reverse fly to address unilateral strength.
Adjust the grip width to target different parts of the upper back.

0601.overview: Using a parallel grip, this reverse fly emphasizes the same posterior shoulder muscles while providing a neutral wrist position, reducing joint strain. It’s ideal for beginners and those with wrist discomfort. The exercise reinforces scapular retraction and upper‑back strength.
0601.exerciseTips:
Maintain a neutral spine and keep the chest lifted.
Pull the handles apart by squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Control the eccentric phase to prevent swinging.
Breath out during the contraction, inhale during the reset.

Switch to an overhand grip for increased trapezius activation.
Do a single‑arm reverse fly to improve side‑to‑side balance.
Add a light pause at peak contraction for greater muscle recruitment.

0603.overview: The seated lever shoulder press develops the deltoids, especially the anterior heads, while also recruiting the triceps and chest for assistance. Keep the back firmly against the pad to prevent arching.
Press upward without locking the elbows fully.
Exhale during the press, inhale while lowering.
Start with a moderate weight to master the range of motion.

Use a neutral grip to reduce shoulder strain.
Perform the press with a slight forward lean to engage the upper chest.
Add a partial range (top half) for deltoid endurance training.

Drive the handles up and slightly forward, avoiding excessive arching.
Breathe out on the push and inhale on the return.
Keep the core engaged to protect the lower back.

Reduce the forward angle for a pure overhead press.
Include a pause at the top to increase time under tension.

0604.overview: The lever shrug isolates the trapezius muscles, helping develop upper‑back width and neck strength. The seated position reduces the need for balance, making it accessible for beginners. Regular shrugs improve posture and shoulder girdle stability.
0604.exerciseTips:
Keep arms straight and focus on lifting the shoulders, not the arms.
Do not roll the shoulders; raise them straight up.
Exhale on the lift, inhale on the descent.
Use a moderate weight to maintain tension throughout the set.
0604.variations:
Perform the shrug with a pause at the top for an isometric hold.
Add a slight forward lean to activate the lower traps.
Use a narrower grip to target the middle trapezius.

0605.overview: The standing lever calf raise strengthens the gastrocnemius and soleus while also engaging ankle stabilizers. The machine’s pads provide a safe loading method for beginners and advanced lifters alike. It improves lower‑leg power for running and jumping.

Keep the core tight to prevent excessive sway.
Rise onto the balls of your feet, fully extending the ankles.
Pause briefly at the top for maximal contraction.
Lower the heels slowly to maintain tension.

Add a hold at the bottom to stretch the calf muscles.

Keep your core muscles engaged and your body stable throughout the exercise.
